verdict.headline: Chip stocks end an eight-day slide, but AI debt worries and bond yields did not ease
verdict.label: Monday close: Nasdaq 26,430.89 (+1.11%), S&P 500 7,690.73 (+0.41%), back above 7,666.45; Dow 51,966.03 (-0.07%); chip index +1.61%; VIX 18.44 (-7.75%); 10Y ~5.07-5.08%; Brent $109.55 (-0.3%), WTI $103.66 (+2.2%); BTC ~$81,840.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the chip index rose 1.61% and ended its longest losing streak since 2008, the Nasdaq gained 1.11% and the S&P 500 closed at 7,690.73, back above the 7,666.45 line it broke on Friday. The gain was narrow: the Dow slipped 0.07% and the Russell 2000 added 0.25%. The largest moves came on analyst calls, led by Amazon's roughly 5% rise after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick. CoreWeave hit a 52-week low and closed slightly lower despite a Goldman Sachs upgrade, and the 10-year yield stayed near 5.07-5.08%.

What it means: Monday reads as relief after the Nasdaq's 4.5% weekly fall rather than an easing of the AI financing worry behind it, since the company at the centre of that worry did not rally and long-term borrowing costs did not fall. The morning report's read held for stocks and bonds but not for oil: Brent gave back nearly all of the Russia waiver's drop to settle at $109.55, and WTI rose 2.2%. Builder confidence fell to 29, the lowest since 2012, which shows rates above 5% weighing on housing as well as AI.

What would change the picture: a close back below 7,666.45 on the S&P 500 would undo Monday's recovery; CoreWeave rising with narrower credit swaps would be the first sign the financing stress is easing. A 10-year below 5.0% would support the rebound; a move toward 5.331% would put rates back at the centre before the October 27-28 Fed meeting. Netflix and SpaceX report Tuesday, Tesla and Meta Wednesday.
verdict.lede_short: Chip stocks ended their longest losing streak since 2008 and the Nasdaq rose 1.1%, putting the S&P 500 back above the level it broke on Friday. The rebound was led by analyst upgrades, though: CoreWeave, the company at the centre of the AI debt worry, closed lower, and the 10-year yield stayed above 5%. A yield under 5% would make the rebound more convincing; Meta's and Tesla's results on Wednesday are the next real test.

supporting_data.label: The Nasdaq rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 0.41% to 7,690.73 while the Dow fell 0.07% — chips ended an eight-day slide, but the buying was about a fifth the size of last week's move out of tech.
The 10-year yield ended little changed near 5.07-5.08% with an October Fed hold priced above 85% — lower hike odds were already in the price, so bonds gave Monday's rebound no help.
Builder confidence fell three points to 29 in October, the lowest since June 2012, with 43% of builders cutting prices — mortgage rates above 7% are now weighing on housing as well as AI financing.

Brent settled 0.3% lower at $109.55 after falling more than $3 intraday, while WTI rose 2.2% to $103.66, its highest since September 15 — the Russia waiver's relief faded as the Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi oil sites.

CoreWeave hit a 52-week low and closed fractionally lower despite a Goldman Sachs upgrade, with credit swaps still at distressed levels — the AI debt worry behind last week's selling did not ease with the chip rebound.
Amazon rose about 5% after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and raised its target to $350, citing 37% AWS growth — the day's largest gains came from rating changes, not new demand data.

trade_setups.thesis: Monday closed 24 points above the line Friday broke; holding it through Wednesday's earnings would make Friday look like an options-expiry move.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back below 7,666.45, especially after Netflix or Meta disappoint, would show Monday's rebound was positioning.

trade_setups.thesis: Chips rose while CoreWeave made a new low, suggesting buyers are choosing the strongest balance sheets rather than the whole AI buildout.
trade_setups.entry: 52-week low set October 19; Friday's close as the first reference above.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close above Friday's level with credit default swaps narrowing would be the first sign the financing stress is easing.

trade_setups.thesis: The 10-year has held above 5% through a 4.5% weekly Nasdaq fall and a 14-year low in builder confidence, so weak data is not pulling it lower.
trade_setups.invalidation: A move under 5.0% would ease housing and AI borrowing; a move toward 5.331% would put rates back at the centre before the October 27-28 Fed meeting.
